# Cleanup API

8 endpoints. Request and response schemas are described on the [schemas page](schemas.md); the other tags are listed in the [API index](README.md).

## Endpoints

### `GET /api/v1/repositories/{name}/cleanup-policies`

List cleanup policies

List cleanup policies for a repository. Requires global admin, or the maintainer or owner role in the repository's project (a caller who cannot read the repository gets 404).

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | string | yes | - |

**Responses**

| Status | Description | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | List of cleanup policies | `application/json`: object |

Fields of the `200` response (`application/json`):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policies` | array of [CleanupPolicy](schemas.md#cleanuppolicy) | no | - |

### `POST /api/v1/repositories/{name}/cleanup-policies`

Create cleanup policy

Create a new cleanup policy for a repository. Requires global admin, or the maintainer or owner role in the repository's project (a caller who cannot read the repository gets 404).

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | string | yes | - |

**Request body** (required)

`application/json`: object

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | - |
| `keep_last_n` | integer | no | Minimum: 1. |
| `keep_since_days` | integer | no | - |
| `name` | string | yes | - |
| `name_pattern` | string | no | - |
| `schedule_cron` | string | no | - |

**Responses**

| Status | Description | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Cleanup policy created | `application/json`: [CleanupPolicy](schemas.md#cleanuppolicy) |

### `POST /api/v1/repositories/{name}/cleanup-policies/{id}/dry-run`

Preview what a cleanup policy would remove (admin; nothing is changed)

Evaluates the policy now with every protection a run applies (immutable releases, release bundles, quarantine, dist-tagged npm versions, the newest build of a maven snapshot) and lists the rows a run would remove or move to the trash. Synchronous; the list is capped at 500 rows.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | string | yes | - |
| `id` | path | string | yes | - |

**Responses**

| Status | Description | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | What a run would remove | `application/json`: [CleanupPreview](schemas.md#cleanuppreview) |
| `default` | Error | `application/json`: [Error](schemas.md#error) |

### `POST /api/v1/repositories/{name}/registry-gc`

Run Docker registry garbage collection now (admin; 409 if already running, 400 if not a docker repository)

Deletes untagged manifests older than the grace period (keeping index children, subjects and referrers of kept manifests) and then the blob records no manifest references any more, freeing their storage once no other repository uses it. Synchronous; the body is optional.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | path | string | yes | - |

**Request body**

`application/json`: [DockerGCRequest](schemas.md#dockergcrequest)

**Responses**

| Status | Description | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | GC report | `application/json`: [DockerGCReport](schemas.md#dockergcreport) |
| `default` | Error | `application/json`: [Error](schemas.md#error) |
